steps.body: A function can be **undone** only if no two inputs share an output — the function is **one-to-one**. Graph version: the **horizontal line test** — if some horizontal line crosses the graph twice, two inputs collide at one output, and no inverse function exists.

widget.prompt: f(x) = x². Give a POSITIVE input that shares its output with x = −3.

commonErrors.feedback: 9 is the shared OUTPUT. The colliding input is the positive x with x² = 9: x = 3.
−3 is the input we started with — the question asks for the OTHER input landing on 9: x = 3.

steps.body: Why the collision kills the inverse.
explanationVariants: An inverse would have to send 9 back to its input — but 9 came from BOTH 3 and −3, and a function can't output two values for one input.
Undoing x² at 9 is ambiguous (3 or −3?), so no inverse FUNCTION exists on the full domain.

widget.prompt: Why does f(x) = x² (all real x) have no inverse function?

options.label: An inverse would need to send 9 to both 3 and −3 — a function can't do that
options.feedback: Exactly — one-to-one failure at even one output makes the reverse assignment ambiguous.

options.label: Because x² has no square root
options.feedback: √9 exists just fine — the problem is that TWO inputs (±3) produce 9, so the reverse direction is ambiguous.

options.label: Because parabolas aren't functions
options.feedback: x² IS a function (it passes the VERTICAL line test). It fails the HORIZONTAL line test, which is what blocks the inverse.

steps.body: Compare y = x³: every horizontal line crosses **once** — outputs are never shared, the cube is one-to-one, and an inverse exists (the cube root). Strictly increasing or strictly decreasing functions always pass the test.

explanationVariants: x³ only ever climbs, so no horizontal line can catch it twice — one-to-one.
Two different inputs always cube to two different values; the graph passes every horizontal line once.

widget.prompt: Which function passes the horizontal line test on its full domain?

options.label: f(x) = x³
options.feedback: Right — strictly increasing, so every output is hit exactly once and the cube root undoes it.

options.label: f(x) = x²
options.feedback: The horizontal line y = 9 crosses at x = ±3 — two hits, test failed.

options.label: f(x) = |x|
options.feedback: y = 4 crosses at x = ±4 — the V shape fails the test just like the parabola.

explanationVariants: |−4| = |4| = 4: two inputs, one output — not one-to-one.
The pair ±4 collides at 4, so |x| can't be undone on its full domain.

widget.prompt: h(x) = |x|. What OUTPUT value do the inputs 4 and −4 collide at?

commonErrors.feedback: |−4| strips the sign: both inputs land at +4.
They land at the SAME output, not the sum: |4| = |−4| = 4.
Only x = 0 maps to 0. The inputs ±4 both map to 4.

explanationVariants: Outputs 5, 8, 5, 11: the output 5 appears for BOTH x = 1 and x = 3 — a collision, so no inverse on this table.
One-to-one requires all outputs distinct; the repeat at 5 fails it.
hints: Scan the OUTPUT row for any repeated value.
x = 1 and x = 3 both matter here — compare their outputs.
f(1) = 5 and f(3) = 5: same output, different inputs. What does that mean for an inverse?

widget.prompt: A table gives f(1)=5, f(2)=8, f(3)=5, f(4)=11. Does f have an inverse function?

options.label: No — the output 5 is shared by x = 1 and x = 3
options.feedback: Right — an inverse can't decide whether 5 should return to 1 or 3.

options.label: Yes — every input has exactly one output
options.feedback: That makes f a FUNCTION, not one-to-one. For an inverse, every OUTPUT must also come from exactly one input, and 5 comes from two.

options.label: No — because 11 appears only once
options.feedback: Appearing once is exactly what one-to-one wants. The failure is the REPEAT: 5 appears twice.

takeaways: One-to-one: no two inputs share an output.
Horizontal line test: any double-crossing line kills the inverse.
Strictly increasing or decreasing functions always pass.
steps.teaser: Next: rescuing x² — restricting the domain until an inverse exists.

concept.body: To test one-to-one from values: look for any repeated OUTPUT. One repeat = not one-to-one = no inverse function.

explanationVariants: g(0) = 2 and g(4) = 2 share the output 2 — that's the collision.
The repeated output is 2, produced by both 0 and 4.

widget.prompt: g(0)=2, g(1)=7, g(4)=2, g(5)=9. Which OUTPUT value is repeated?

commonErrors.feedback: 4 is an INPUT. Scan the outputs: 2, 7, 2, 9 — the 2 repeats.
7 appears once (from x = 1). The output 2 appears twice, from x = 0 and x = 4.
